Thanks all!

messages.body_plain:
D-RUG,

I am hosting a seminar and workshop that may be of interest to you all. See the attached flyers for details. These workshops are tied to work I've been doing to teach dynamics from a computational perspective and an interactive textbook that my co-instructors and I have been developing. Prof. Allen Downey's work has been a significant influence to mine. Please share widely. I also forgot to mention that if you are interested in meeting with Allen or joining for lunch/dinner activities, let me know.

Jason
moorepants.info <http://moorepants.info>
+01 530-601-9791

messages.subject: Multivariate longitudinal/repeated measures non-parametric ANOVA?
messages.body_plain:
Multivariate longitudinal/repeated measures non-parametric ANOVA?

Anyone familiar with a tool like this in R?

I have been using nparLD (Response~Time*Season*Habitat) but it only allows for two way. Would like to find one that would allow for:

Response ~ Time(RepeatedMeasure)*Sex*Repro*Season*Habitat

Any thoughts?

Thanks!

Katie

--

PhD Candidate

Davis, CA 95616

messages.subject: predict function linking metafor:rma.mv with glmulti?
messages.subject_clean: predict function linking metafor:rma.mv with glmulti?
messages.body_plain:
I'm using the metafor package to build meta-analysis models - specifically, the rma.mv <http://rma.mv>() function since I have some random effects.  I also have a few predictor (modifier) variables and am using glmulti to explore their relationships to the effect size (via multi-model averaging as described here <http://www.metafor-project.org/doku.php/tips:model_selection_with_glmulti>, which gives me a table of averaged coefficients).

I would now like to make predictions for a new set of predictor variable values, using the multi-model averaged parameters.  I realize I can calculate the predicted effect size itself using the averaged coefficients directly, but I'd also like to have confidence intervals for the predicted effect size, and I'm not sure of the correct way to get those.  rma.mv <http://rma.mv>() itself has a predict function, so I can easily get predictions + CIs for the best model returned by glmulti, but for the particular question I'm asking, I think multi-model averaged predictions would be better.

The attached vignette suggests that I may need to write a custom predict function that links glmulti and rma.mv <http://rma.mv>.  Before I wade into that, thought I'd check here to see whether anyone has done this already?

Thanks so much for any suggestions!
Kelly
